outcome: No progress found since 26 January 2024: no (2,5)-perfect number (n with σ(σ(n)) = 5n) has been found or proven not to exist, and no paper, preprint, or database update addressing this specific case was located.
summary: This bullet asks whether any (2,5)-perfect number exists, i.e. an n with σ(σ(n)) = 5n, in the (m,k)-perfect generalization of superperfect numbers (σ^m(n) = kn) documented on the Wikipedia 'Superperfect number' article and in MathWorld's 'Multiperfect Number' / 'Superperfect Number' pages. Both sources give a table of (2,k)-perfect numbers with known examples for k = 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 (with OEIS sequences A019279–A019291, skipping A019280 which would be k=5) but no entry and no known example for k = 5 — this is the specific gap the Wikipedia bullet is asking about. I searched arXiv and general web sources for any 2024–2026 work naming '(2,5)-perfect', 'σ(σ(n))=5n', or 'sigma_2(n)=5n' and found nothing addressing this case. Related but distinct recent papers were checked and ruled out as off-topic: 'On near superperfect numbers, the Goormaghtigh conjecture, and Mertens' theorem' (arXiv:2505.08160, May 2025) studies numbers with σ(σ(n)) = 2n + d (a near-(2,2)-perfect variant, not (2,5)); 'On Characterizing Potential Friends of 20' (arXiv:2409.04451) discusses '7/5-perfect'-type ratios of a single σ application, not the iterated σ(σ(n))=5n condition; 'Odd Spoof Multiperfect Numbers' (arXiv:2502.16954, Feb 2025) generalizes spoof/Descartes-style multiperfect numbers (single σ, k-perfect) rather than iterated (m,k)-perfect numbers. None of these, nor any other source found, discusses k=5 with m=2. The live Wikipedia 'Superperfect number' article's (m,k)-perfect table appears unchanged from the frozen revision in this respect (same gap at (2,5)), consistent with no update having been made. This is a small, obscure sub-case of multiperfect-number theory that appears to have attracted essentially no dedicated research attention in the window, and certainly none involving AI systems.
competing_reading: It is conceivable that a paper computing (2,k)-perfect numbers for a range of k (e.g. an updated computational survey of iterated-sigma multiperfect numbers) exists in a venue not indexed by the search engines used, and either extended the search bound for (2,5) or found none up to some limit without explicitly using the '(2,5)-perfect' phrase, using different notation (e.g. 'iterated sum-of-divisors' or a table without prose calling out k=5 by name) that these searches missed.
what_would_settle_it: A full-text search of the actual (not AI-summarized) content of arXiv papers on multiply-iterated sigma functions and multiperfect numbers published 2024–2026, and confirmation from OEIS that no sequence exists for (2,5)-perfect numbers (i.e., that A019280 is reserved for (2,2)-perfect/superperfect and no other identifier has been created for k=5).
